gun noun

Traupman 187: rifle

sclopētum, sclopētī n.

noun, second declension

a gun, a rifle

From Italian schioppetto, in Latin since the Renaissance (M-O). A hunting rifle is sclopētum vēnātōrium (M-O, Egger); a pistol sclopētum minus (M-O, Busbecq). To fire a gun is sclopētāre (Traupman 324) or sclopētum displōdere (M-O s.v. shoot).

Other words

  • tormentum, tormentī n. — a big gun, a cannon; classically a catapult

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 2.8 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 187; M-O s.v. cannon

    Classically an engine that hurls missiles, a catapult or ballista (Caes. B.G. 2.8), and the missile it throws; the Renaissance writers used it for artillery (M-O), and so does Traupman. Not for a handgun. Its other common sense is torture, or the rack.

  • sclopētō, sclopētāre — fire a gun, shoot

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 324
